rv.q: It's tremendous production of a play that, in Proctor's cry 'Is the accuser always holy now?', retains its disturbing relevance.
All in all the Old Vic became the perfect setting that really did justice to the sheer brilliance of Miller’s writing.
But a lot of the noise is too hollow to hurt, too blustery to burn.
Farber’s production reminds us of The Crucible’s potency.
Freeman’s low-key, conversational Richard has integrity but no excitement and the play is driven by the more spirited performances of Gerald Kyd as Catesby and Jo-Stone-Fewings as Buckingham.

cn.t: Farber's revelatory production of Miller's witch-hunt classic earns praise, with Armitage delivering a rock-solid central performance, though critics remain divided on the overall execution.
